cells.tense: Right now you are holding your read of a situation steady and the timing to say it.
cells.ask: Say the one clear thing you've been sitting on, to the person it concerns, before the week ends.
cells.core:
This is the thing going right: you take in a situation, find the words that carry it, and pick the hour it can be heard in. Not blunt, not silent. People leave a conversation with you clearer than they arrived, and most of them can't say why.

The edge is small. There is a thing you've been sitting on, and the practice is handing it over once, to the person it concerns. Say it plainly this week — not because the moment is perfect, but because the moment you're waiting for may not arrive. Then notice what holding your read this exact actually costs you. That cost is what keeps the timing honest instead of careful.
cells.sheetLine: You time the truth so it can be heard.

cells.tense: You are reading this arrangement further ahead than anyone needs you to, bracing for how it lands.
cells.ask: When you catch yourself arguing a point past the room, close your mouth and ask one real question instead.
cells.core:
Going well, you read a room accurately and say what you see while it's still alive; people move with you. Tilted the other way, you stop steering and start predicting. Every arrangement gets read three moves out, every sentence weighed for how it will land, and the reading outruns the room. Someone says a simple thing and you are already three reasons past them.

That far ahead, you're annotating people instead of being with them. The direction you actually want comes from feeling your way through the conversation, not from staying ahead of it. When you catch yourself rehearsing a point past where anyone is, stop mid-sentence and ask one real question. Let the quiet after it be yours too.

cells.tense: You have been holding your read back somewhere, and it is still standing there waiting.
cells.ask: Tell one person the half-formed thing you noticed about them, without checking it first.
cells.core:
Working, a read arrives, words come, and it lands in the room on time. People walk away from you with something they can use. Run dry, the read shows up and doesn't come out — not lost, just unspoken, held at a threshold you passed without crossing. The clarity stays private and the moment slides by, and after enough of those you stop expecting the words at all.

Forcing it out isn't the answer. Be with one person and let what you notice about them actually land. Tell them the half-formed version — the unfinished read, not the finished judgment. They'll meet it or they won't, and either way something loosens. Warmth with another person is what gives your thinking somewhere to arrive.

cells.tense: You are already handling the read and the timing and calling it just how the conversation went.
cells.ask: Put your name on one call you made this week — say it to someone, even to yourself out loud.
cells.core:
When it's visible, you read what's off, decide what's fair, and choose the moment — and it's plainly yours. In the shadow, the same work runs in the room and gets filed under nobody. You say the conversation went that way, or that it needed handling. The shape is real. The hand is missing.

That's what wears on you. You make the call on what gets said and when, and it goes unclaimed. Say so about one call from this week — out loud, even alone. What you've claimed you can hand to someone else, and a person near you could use the version you'd have edited out.
